newsitem.title: UK: Toddler's lip stitched back after dog bites it off.
newsitem.headline: Toddler's lip stitched back after dog bites it off.

text.p: A toddler whose lip was ripped off by a large dog will smile again -- doctors stitched it back after it was found in the animal's stomach.

Three-year-old Megan MacFarlane, of Arbroath in east Scotland, was eating ice cream outside her house when a bull mastiff ripped off her lip, said a spokesman for the Dundee Royal Infirmary, the hospital which treated her.

"As her mother said later: 'She was in the wrong place at the wrong time.' We don't think it was an act of aggression by the dog. It was thirsty after a walk and leapt up at the ice cream," the spokesman told Reuters.

The dog's owner immediately offered to have the mastiff put down by a vet, who found the piece of lip in the dog's stomach. He cleaned the tissue, put it in saline and ice and had it rushed to the hospital.
The vet had searched for the missing piece of lip after police had been unable to find it. Without it, the girl faced permanent disfigurement.
The plastic surgeon, who performed the operation, expected to know within 48-hours whether the graft had bonded successfully, the spokesman said.
